population.note: FICTIONAL. The adult population is about 278M. Current users are 39.0% (≈108.4M) and ever-users 52.0% (≈144.6M), so 13.0 points (≈36.1M) used and are off now, and ≈133.6M have never used. Ever-use rose 12.0 points against a limit of 13.5. Cycling arithmetic: about 20.5 points of adults are current users on a second or later course, and about 5.5 points are off-now users who restarted at least once and stopped again. (20.5 + 5.5)/52.0 = 50.0% have cycled. That fits ~35% one-year persistence on weeklies and 36–47% restart within a year. The off-now 13.0 points are roughly 5.5 repeat stoppers and 7.5 single-course stoppers. Age check: 18–29: 22% × 52M = 11.4M; 30–49: 43% × 92M = 39.6M; 50–64: 56% × 62M = 34.7M; 65+: 31.5% × 72M = 22.7M. Total 108.4M = 39.0%. Income thirds average (41 + 40 + 36)/3 = 39.0. The bottom third gained most (+11.5 points), mainly through the 2035 Medicaid medication-only coverage (≈6.2M enrollees) and the nine new continuation-standard states. Imports are concentrated in the ten holdout states. Of the ≈36.1M off now, about 9M are on a bone pause or stopped after a DEXA result, 3M+ stopped over NAION workups or GI problems, and the rest stopped over price, gating, tenure gaps or choice. The ≈133.6M never-users skew to under-30s, people with contraindications, residents of holdout states and refusers by conviction. Off-drug adults in their 50s now get asked why. Pediatric: 1.8% of ≈73M ≈ 1.31M children, ≈1.12M aged 12–17 and ≈190k aged 6–11, most of the latter on Medicaid EPSDT since the Dec 2035 approval. About one child in two lives with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Part D obesity benefit statutory terms unchanged: $199/month negotiated rate, $50 copay, counselling visit, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity. The May 2035 reconciliation law made acceptance of the $199 rate a condition of Part D and Medicaid listing for every incretin, which brought MariTide (monthly) onto formularies in Sep 2035. Medicare pays 19.4% of fills, ≈21.0M users (≈19.2M aged 65+ and ≈1.8M disabled under-65): ≈9.2M for diabetes and ≈11.8M for obesity. Obesity-benefit spend: 11.8M × $199 × 12 ≈ $28.2B gross, less copays of 11.8M × $50 × 12 ≈ $7.1B, ≈$21.1B net to the program. All Medicare incretin fills: 21.0M × $199 × 12 ≈ $50.1B gross. Medicaid: 40 states plus DC now use the 90% match and continuation standard, up from 31 plus DC. 23 of them also adopted the new optional 'metabolic medication-only' eligibility group for adults up to 200% FPL, modelled on family-planning limited-benefit coverage. Medicaid pays 21.2% of fills, ≈23.0M users (≈6.2M of them medication-only enrollees) × $199 × 12 ≈ $54.9B gross: ≈$49.4B federal, ≈$5.5B state, before supplemental rebates. Public programs combined pay 40.6% of fills (≈44.0M users), more than employers (30.4%) for the first time.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month domestically, including generic oral semaglutide. Export pricing to US parcels has roughly doubled under the 2035 tariff. The Telangana first-filer plant is still under US import alert. China: generic semaglutide, tirzepatide copies and 'research' retatrutide, still the API base of the gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 50–80. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics. US: the mid-2035 contingent date for rival filers passed with no launch. A district court has stayed FDA approval of rivals while the first filer contests a forfeiture determination, and two rival filers say the 100% tariff on their Indian-made sterile product makes launch uneconomic anyway. The appeal is expected in 2037. Tirzepatide exclusivity runs later.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Shock up, second step running. A Section 232 tariff increase in Jan 2035 (to 100% on finished sterile injectables and on incretin API from India and China) came with another ≈$50 rise in direct-portal maintenance prices. Current cash prices: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $299–379; Wegovy pill 50 mg $349; oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) still $149–150; retatrutide $499 direct and $1,799 list; amycretin $549; MariTide $599/month direct. Gray parcels: Indian pens $45–80, up from $20–30, because of tariffs on declared value and seizures. Commercial PBM net ≈$225–245. Payer mix of 108.4M users: Medicare 21.0M (19.4%), Medicaid 23.0M (21.2%), commercial 33.0M (30.4%), cash/direct 20.5M (18.9%, including ≈3.6M 'calm'/'focus' subscribers, down from 4.6M), imported/counterfeit 10.9M (10.1%). Sum = 108.4M. Employer coverage fell to 58%. About 88% of covering plans are gated, and about 40% of those use tenure gates. Some employers now steer low-wage staff to the Medicaid medication-only group. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand. Routes: ≈38% daily oral, ≈10% monthly MariTide (≈11M, about 5.5M of them publicly paid, many pharmacy-administered), ≈52% weekly injectable.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The monthly_or_implant driver is met by an existing product in new forms and by coverage, not by a new molecule. In Sep 2035 MariTide entered Part D and Medicaid at the statutory $199 rate. In Feb 2036 FDA approved an every-8-weeks maintenance dose (sBLA filed Jan 2035). Pharmacist-administered 'shot day' clinics now provide most publicly paid monthly doses. No implant is on the market. The pediatric_under_12 driver is met by a semaglutide sNDA filed Nov 2034 on a 68-week trial in ages 6–11 (≈17% BMI reduction versus placebo), approved Dec 2035, 13 months after filing. The label requires growth-velocity monitoring and baseline and annual DEXA. Survodutide's MASH sNDA, under review at the start, was approved Sep 2035. A bimagrumab/semaglutide combination was filed Mar 2036 and is under review, with no decision possible before Mar 2037. Lilly's next-generation orals are still in development and unfiled. Incretin market ≈$262B in 2036. US ≈$240B: (108.4M − 10.9M imports) = 97.5M paying users × ≈$205 blended net × 12 ≈ $239.9B. The blend is pulled down by public fills at $199. Ex-US ≈$22B.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Planned dose holidays on weeklies produce restart nausea.
Rising in absolute numbers with a user base of 108M and more 65+ users.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Gray-product overdosing confounds reports.

Now treated as a recognised population problem. ≈2.7M long-term Medicare users meet sarcopenia criteria, up from 1.6M. Lean mass is ~30–40% of loss in untrained users over 50. Grip-strength decline appears in national aging surveys.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Oct 2035 class Warnings and Precautions upgrade on lean mass and bone across all incretins. CMS now requires baseline DEXA plus protein and resistance-training counselling at the Part D visit for users 65+ and postmenopausal women.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈12.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 12.5M × ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 26,250 excess hip fractures a year, against ~320,000 US total. CDC reports the age-adjusted 65+ hip-fracture rate rose ~3% over 2033–35 after three decades of decline. Cost ≈ 26,250 × ~$48,000 (hospital plus rehabilitation) ≈ $1.26B/yr, mostly Part A and Medicare Advantage. The vertebral tail in cycling women 50–64 continues. DEXA waits are 8–14 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning upgraded Oct 2035, not boxed. CMS continuation standard amended: a mandatory 90-day bone pause at T-score ≤ −2.5 unless an antiresorptive is co-prescribed. Bone endpoints required in all filings. DOJ civil case against Novo still unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: RR ≈1.7. At ~4 per 100,000 baseline across ≈108M users, ≈3,000 excess cases a year, mostly partial and permanent monocular loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class W&P (May 2034) retained; Medication Guide; MDL consolidated. Not boxed.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The ~12% vs ~5% figure at 12 mg retatrutide stands. ≈12M people are on top-dose triple or dual regimens, which implies roughly 840k excess cases if the association is causal. Pharmacy claims show about a third of weekly users take at least one planned holiday of two weeks or more a year. Monthly users cannot titrate quickly. There is still no randomised low-dose measurement; an NIH crossover trial is enrolling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FTC consent orders stand. Eleven states restrict mood and focus marketing. No label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mandatory bone pauses now add a medically forced stop stream of ≈9M people off on bone grounds over the window.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The CMS bone-pause code no longer counts against continuation. Private gated plans still vary.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency, common in high-loss older users and gray users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Folded into the Part D counselling template; pediatric label requires a nutrition plan.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About 14 years of follow-up. The 2035 adolescent readout found BMD accrual ~2–3% below matched controls at 2 years, with partial catch-up after weight stabilises and no fracture excess yet. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements extended to 2039 for adolescents.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈10.9M import or counterfeit users, up from 7.1M. Poison-centre calls are up a further ~25% on 2034. No new mass-contamination cluster this step, but scattered abscess and dosing-error cases continue in holdout states.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts and seizures continue. Safe Pens bill still stalled. No individual prosecutions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging. Pressed fakes are a stable share of seizures, with 0–300% of labelled content. Harms are GI and hypoglycaemia.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ long-term users. Sarcopenia and NAION are cited cofactors.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D visit, now paired with strength testing.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging on DEXA cohorts of 2033 shortage and gating stoppers, concentrated in women 50–64.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint endocrine and geriatrics guidance (2035) recommends resistance training before any planned stop. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide; significance unclear.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Precautionary label; CV outcomes trial ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth velocity and bone accrual in children under 12
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. ≈190k children aged 6–11 are on drug. Trial data show slightly reduced height velocity during the dose-escalation phase, and it is unclear whether this recovers. No long-term data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label requires growth-velocity and annual DEXA monitoring plus a registry PMR. Eleven states limit prescribing to specialists after an in-person visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Prolonged adverse effects on long-acting monthly dosing (MariTide)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Because of the antibody half-life, GI intolerance or a NAION workup cannot be ended by skipping a dose, and washout takes weeks. Complaints are rising with pharmacy-administered public use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label language on washout; CMS lets pharmacists defer a dose without counting it against PDC.

food_and_beverage.state: With 39% of adults on the drug, salty-snack volume is falling ~5% a year and confectionery ~6%. Two private-equity candy portfolios have merged to cut overhead. Protein-forward and calcium/vitamin-D 'bone' lines grew sharply after the Oct 2035 warning and the CMS counselling change. Kroger and Meijer stores in Dayton and Columbus stock 'shot-day' protein bundles near the pharmacy counter. Calorie-dense value packs still sell in holdout-state discount grocers.

alcohol.state: Ninth straight year of spirits volume decline; beer down; NA and single-serve formats hold. Bar traffic falls fastest in high-uptake suburbs.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat to slightly down. Spend per cover is down ~13% from 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Gram-priced protein bowls are standard, and half-portion menus are a default rather than an option. Value buffets keep closing outside holdout states.

apparel.state: 'Structured' and 'cycle' ranges are industry-wide. Mid-market plus-size inventory keeps shrinking. Resale sized for cycling is growing, and 'bone pause' capsule wardrobes (stretch waists for a 90-day regain) are a small category at Kohl's and Target.

fitness.state: Growing fastest of any sector. CMS counselling now prescribes resistance training, Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' benefits have spread, and DEXA-plus-coaching chains open in strip malls. The constraint is still trainers qualified for frail older lifters, and community colleges in Ohio and Arizona run 12-week certificates.

insurance.state: Employer coverage fell to 58% after the second price rise. ~88% of covering plans are gated and about 40% of those use tenure gates. Some employers point low-wage staff to Medicaid medication-only coverage. Pharmacy trend ~+12%. Bone, fall and eye costs land on Part A and MA, and the hip-fracture excess alone is ≈$1.26B/yr. Life insurers price untreated BMI and now DEXA T-scores.

pharma.state: US volume up ~37% over two years. Private net up ~6%, while the public $199 rate holds the blended net near $205. Amgen gains most from MariTide's public listing. Lilly leads the high-dose segment, and Novo leads orals and pediatrics. US generic semaglutide is still blocked. Indian exporters lose some parcel volume to tariffs and seizures. Bone-drug makers (antiresorptives) see a co-prescribing boom.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on it signals nothing, and being visibly off invites a question. Shape still signals income: trained shoulders mean a coached regimen; a soft 'pill body' means the middle; a pharmacy shot-day body, lean with thin arms, often means Medicaid; visible regain means a holdout state, a tenure gap or a bone pause. The bone pause has become a recognised, sympathetic reason to be off, the one excuse nobody questions.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use rates have nearly converged, at 36% in the bottom third against 41% at the top, because Medicaid now pays for so many. Bodies still diverge on muscle, not fat. The divide is no longer whether you can get the drug. It is whether you also get the trainer and the DEXA follow-up. Women 50–64 in Dayton and the Phoenix west side carry most of the cycling-regain and vertebral-fracture burden.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals are simply how people eat at family gatherings. Hosts set out small plates by default and ask nobody. Church potlucks and Sunday full-table dinners in Memphis and Houston persist as heritage, and on-drug relatives now attend them for the company and leave food on their plates without comment.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps have dropped the on/off field as redundant and added 'regimen' and 'holiday-friendly'. 'Off by choice' is now something people feel they must explain on a profile. Advice columns field complaints about partners on monthly shots who can no longer take a weekend holiday.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Medicalised and assumed managed. Appetite shown in public, such as a second plate or a dessert eaten alone, reads as either a holiday or a lapse. The backlash coalition is roughly the same absolute size but shrinking as a share. It has found common cause with parents' groups over the pediatric approval.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. 12 mg retatrutide figures stand at ~12% versus ~5% of comparators. ≈12M people on top-dose triple or dual regimens imply ≈840k excess cases if causal. Claims data show ~one-third of weekly users take at least one planned holiday of two weeks or more a year. The 'calm' subscriber base fell from 4.6M to ≈3.6M under state restrictions. Monthly users (≈11M) report the grey more often in surveys, possibly because they cannot titrate. No randomised low-dose data yet.
interior_life.framing: A side effect you manage, like the fog on antihistamines. 'The grey' is a talk-show word, prescribers write 'dose holiday' in charts, and the 'calm' brands have drifted their language toward 'steady'. The complaint is common, and almost nobody treats it as a reason to stop.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Dose-down before sales peaks is routine on weeklies. Workers who move to publicly paid monthly shots lose that control and some switch back to weeklies. In 2036 a national nurses' union contract and the largest PBM recognised planned holidays of up to 4 weeks as not counting against adherence gates. Tenure gates still tie warehouse staff to jobs. Some employers now offer 'grey days' as unofficial leave.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The grey has become a mainstream subject. A network sitcom's running gag is a husband timing his holidays to his band's gigs. 'Written on holiday' has replaced 'written unmedicated' as the Nashville badge. High-stimulus leisure keeps growing. Indie film has moved from pen sellers to the pharmacy shot-day line.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen routinely for regimen and holiday schedule. Couples coordinate holidays around anniversaries and trips. Partners on monthly antibody shots cannot join a holiday, which is a new and frequent counselling complaint.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Prices and tariffs dominate. The 2035 reconciliation law is claimed by both parties. The pediatric approval and the grey together drove a restriction coalition of parents'-rights conservatives and public-health progressives, which passed eleven state laws. The 2036 presidential campaign argues over the tariff, which makes a domestic generic less likely and parcels dearer.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and cautious. It approved pediatric 6–11 with growth and DEXA PMRs, approved survodutide for MASH and MariTide every-8-weeks maintenance, and upgraded the class warning on lean mass and bone in Oct 2035, without a box. It still brings no individual import prosecutions. Congress passed coverage but no importation or authentication law.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The May 2035 reconciliation law kept the $199 Part D rate and $50 copay. It made acceptance of the statutory rate a condition of Part D and Medicaid listing for every incretin, extended the 90% match indefinitely, and created an optional Medicaid medication-only eligibility group for adults to 200% FPL. Nine states joined the continuation standard (40 plus DC), and 23 adopted the medication-only group. Ten states hold out, including Texas and Florida. There is no individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Continuation standard: ≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weights, 5% response or clinician override, two misses suspend coverage for 6 months. It now also requires a mandatory bone pause at T ≤ −2.5 absent an antiresorptive, and baseline DEXA with strength testing for 65+ and postmenopausal women. Pharmacy-administered monthly shots log adherence automatically and are becoming the default proof of PDC for Medicaid medication-only enrollees. Indiana and Arkansas keep their 12-month rules. Private kiosk-weight premium tiers continue under the wellness-surcharge allowance. Restriction: eleven states (including California, New York, Illinois and Utah) limit under-12 prescribing to pediatric specialists after an in-person visit, set 18 as the minimum age for non-obesity 'calm'/'focus' prescribing, require an in-person exam for those prescriptions, and ban incretin advertising aimed at minors.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers to tirzepatide. Fleets keep voluntary visual-field checks, and FMCSA has added no rule. The Army now grants accession waivers to recruits stable for 12 months on monthly dosing, but not on weeklies, citing field logistics. The Air Force continues waivers.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Jan 2035 Section 232 increase to 100% on Indian and Chinese incretin API and finished sterile injectables raised parcel prices and gave rival generic filers a reason to delay. India has opened a WTO consultation and calls the tariff and the Telangana import alert one protectionist policy. Chinese API still underlies most gray product. Novo and Lilly cite tariffs and US fill-finish buildout for the portal increases.

events.event: The administration raises Section 232 tariffs to 100% on incretin API and finished sterile injectables from India and China. Within weeks Novo and Lilly add about $50 a month to direct-portal maintenance prices, Indian parcel pens rise from $20–30 to $45–80, and in July the mid-2035 generic semaglutide date passes with no launch because a court stays rival approvals during the first filer's forfeiture fight

Congress's budget reconciliation law extends the 90% Medicaid incretin match indefinitely and creates an optional medication-only Medicaid eligibility group for adults up to 200% FPL. It also requires every incretin to accept the $199 statutory rate to be listed. Nine states join the continuation standard by year end, and Amgen's monthly MariTide enters Part D and Medicaid in September, delivered largely through pharmacy 'shot days'. Public programs now pay for more fills than employers

CDC reports that the age-adjusted hip-fracture rate among Americans 65+ rose about 3% over two years, the first sustained rise in three decades. The same month FDA upgrades the class warning on lean-mass and bone loss, and CMS makes a 90-day bone pause mandatory at osteoporotic T-scores unless an antiresorptive is co-prescribed

FDA approves weekly semaglutide for children aged 6 to 11 with obesity, requiring growth-velocity monitoring and annual bone scans. Medicaid EPSDT coverage follows automatically, and pediatric endocrinology waitlists in Ohio and Georgia stretch past six months

Utah and California become the ninth and tenth of eleven states to enact incretin restrictions. The laws limit under-12 prescribing to specialists after an in-person visit, set 18 as the minimum age for 'calm' and 'focus' prescriptions, require an in-person exam for them, and ban incretin advertising aimed at minors. 'Quiet' and 'Even' geofence their apps out of the restricting states

The largest PBM announces that planned dose holidays of up to four weeks will no longer count against adherence gates in commercial plans, a month after a national nurses' union contract wrote 'grey days' into its scheduling terms. Claims data show a third of weekly users take at least one holiday a year

open_tensions: Public programs now pay 40.6% of fills at a frozen $199. Manufacturers recover margin from employers and cash buyers, and employers respond with tenure gates and by steering low-wage staff to Medicaid medication-only coverage. Public budgets absorb the growth (≈$105B gross across Medicare and Medicaid), and nobody scores the ≈$1.26B a year in excess hip fractures against it.

The 100% tariff makes parcel pens dearer and a domestic generic less likely at the same time. ≈10.9M Americans, concentrated in the ten holdout states, still use imported or counterfeit product. The forfeiture appeal, the Safe Pens bill and a WTO consultation are all unresolved.

Monthly pharmacy-administered shots solve adherence for Medicaid and turn every dose into a verification record. They also remove the dose holiday, the main way people manage the grey, just as the grey has become a mainstream complaint and the PBM began recognising holidays.

Semaglutide is approved for 6–11-year-olds with an unresolved growth signal and a 2–3% adolescent bone-accrual lag. Medicaid EPSDT must cover it, eleven states restrict who may prescribe it, and specialist waitlists mean the restriction works as rationing, falling hardest on Medicaid children in the restricting states.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 beneficiary copay, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.
The 503B compounding exclusion and the 503A injunction still stand.
The FTC consent orders still bar 'anxiety treatment' claims while permitting 'calm' and 'focus' language for subscription brands.

prose.headline: Medicaid Pays for the Shot Now. Nobody Asks Why You're On It. They Ask Why You Stopped.
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2036 almost four American adults in ten are on an incretin drug, and more than half have tried one. Among people in their fifties the majority is now on it. Being on it is like wearing reading glasses: it says nothing about you. Being off it at fifty-five gets a gentle question at the dinner table, and usually the answer is a bone scan.

The bones are this step's story. For thirty years American hip-fracture rates fell. In October 2035 the CDC reported that they had risen for two years running among people over sixty-five. Twelve and a half million older Americans have now been on these drugs for more than two years. Even a modest excess risk at that scale comes to about twenty-six thousand extra broken hips a year. The FDA strengthened the class warning. Medicare now orders a ninety-day pause when a scan shows osteoporosis, unless the patient also takes a bone drug, and requires a strength test and a talk about protein at every counselling visit. Gyms that can train frail lifters are the fastest-growing business in the Midwest.

Prices went up again. In January 2035 the administration doubled tariffs on Indian and Chinese drug ingredients and sterile injectables, and Novo and Lilly added another fifty dollars a month to maintenance prices. The generic semaglutide that was supposed to arrive in mid-2035 did not. A court froze rival approvals while the first filer fought to keep its exclusivity, and the rivals' Indian-made product now carries a 100% tariff. Parcel pens from Hyderabad that cost twenty-five dollars now cost sixty. Nearly eleven million Americans still buy them, mostly in Texas, Florida and the other states that stayed out.

The price shock also produced the largest public expansion yet. That spring's budget law made the ninety percent federal match permanent and let states cover the drug alone, with no other Medicaid benefits, for working adults up to twice the poverty line. It also required every incretin, including Amgen's monthly shot, to accept Medicare's $199 rate or lose the public market. Amgen accepted. Forty states and DC now run the program, and public programs pay for more prescriptions than employers do. Some employers have noticed and point their low-wage workers toward Medicaid.

A monthly shot has changed what adherence means. Pharmacies in Dayton and Tucson run shot days, a line on the first Tuesday of the month, and each injection is logged as proof of compliance. Nobody has to remember a weekly pen, and nobody can skip one either. That matters because the grey, the flattening of pleasure that people on high doses describe, has become an ordinary complaint, discussed on talk shows and in sitcoms. The usual remedy is a dose holiday, which on a weekly pen means skipping a week or two. A third of weekly users now take one each year, and in June the largest pharmacy benefit manager stopped counting them against adherence. On a monthly antibody a holiday is not possible.

In December the FDA approved semaglutide for children aged six to eleven, with growth checks and yearly bone scans. Older children's bones had been building about two to three percent less density than expected. The approval brought together parents'-rights conservatives and public-health progressives. Eleven states now limit prescribing to young children to specialists, set eighteen as the minimum age for the calm and focus subscriptions, and ban advertising aimed at minors. In Ohio, a pediatric endocrinology appointment takes seven months.

None of this looks like a crisis. The country is eating less, drinking less and lifting more, and more of its hips are breaking. Medicaid now pays for most low-income adults' shots, and many of those adults are also the ones not getting the strength training and bone follow-up.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Lorraine Pruitt, fifty-eight, does her first client in Huber Heights at seven: compression socks, pill sorter, a man who calls her by his late wife's name. Lunch is half a turkey wrap in the car. She saves the other half for later out of habit, though she won't eat it.

At two she joins the shot-day line at the Kroger pharmacy on Wilmington Pike, behind a man in a FedEx vest and a teenager with her mother. The pharmacist scans Lorraine's Medicaid card, the medication-only kind she got last spring when her agency dropped her plan. Four-dollar copay. He reads her DEXA result off the screen: minus 2.3. 'Close,' he says. 'Do your exercises, or next time it's a pause.' She has the printout of exercises in her glovebox. The shot stings less than the Indian pens did. Those came in a padded envelope, and she checked the lot numbers against a Telegram list.

At the register, the protein bundle is on sale. She buys two.

Her sister Tammy calls while she drives. Tammy is off, after the eye thing, and still has to tell people at church about the eye thing. 'They look at my plate like I've given up,' Tammy says.

At six her granddaughter Kaylee, nine, does homework at the kitchen table. The pediatrician has mentioned the new shot twice. The specialist's earliest appointment is in March. Lorraine's daughter hasn't decided whether to keep it.

Kaylee eats a second helping of mac and cheese. Lorraine watches her eat it and says nothing about it.
